4 اعزب He made to be distant, or remote; or to go far away. (K, * TA.) You say, اعزبهُ ٱللّٰهُ God made him, or may God make him, to go away, or far away. (S, TA.) ―
-b2- اعزب الإِبِلَ He drove the camels to a distance in the pasturage, not to return in the evening. (TA.) And اعزب إِبِلَهُ and ↓ عزّبها He made his camels to pass the night in the pasturage, not bringing them back in the evening. (TA.) And اعزب جَمَلَهُ is like أَضَلَّهُ [He made his camel to go astray]. (A.) ―
-b3- [Hence,] اعزب ٱللّٰهُ عَنْهُ حِلْمَهُ (assumed tropical:) God made his forbearance to become remote from him. (O.) ―
-b4- And أَعْزَبْنَا الكَلَأَ, (O,) or أَعْزَبْنَا alone, (S,) We lighted upon remote herbage. (S, O.) ＝
-A2- As intrans.: see 1, first sentence: and the same in the latter half. ―
-b2- [Hence,] اعزب القَوْمُ The people's camels went away to a distance in the pasturage, not to return in the evening. (S, * O, * K, * TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
